method.realPath: real Claude Code hook payload -> kai-hook.exe (the REAL relay binary) -> named pipe \\.\pipe\kai-<sid> -> app/src-tauri/src/pipe.rs -> app.emit("hook") -> app/src/island/hooks.ts handleHook -> island.observeWorkerActivity(type,payload) -> KaiRuntimeMachine.applyEvent -> onTransition -> State.setRuntime -> State.notify -> island.sync -> engine.setState(faceState()) -> KaiEngine/Orb -> canvas
method.rendererReceipt: The character's OWN renderer handle (window.__kaiEngine, registered inside KaiEngine.draw()) is read over CDP: .state (what engine.setState received, lower-cased) and .renderer.pose (the pose the Orb was driven to via poseForState()). This is the receipt that the RENDERER received the state, not a DOM guess.
method.screenshots: Page.captureScreenshot of the running island window (1035x460, DPR 1.435); each analysed with vision_analyze on a crop of the pill. Hashes alone are not proof; the descriptions below are what the model SAW.
method.noTimers: No setTimeout triggers a state. Every non-IDLE state is entered by a real hook event delivered over the real pipe. (setTimeout appears only in the IDLE reset wait, which merely WAITS for the bounded result-hold safeguard to elapse.)

states.finding: REAL WIRING GAP, three links missing: (1) core/src/runtime.ts calls notifications.notify({type:'mission.recovery_blocked'}), which core/src/notifications/service.ts publishes on the wire as event type 'notification.created' (the recovery type rides inside the payload as payload.type). stateForEvent() switches on event.type, so the 'mission.recovery_blocked' branch can NEVER fire. (2) app/src/core/core-state.ts:139 CoreEventRow carries only {id,type,at,text} — the payload is consumed for the text and NOT retained, so the recovery type is lost at the reducer. (3) app/src/island/core-bridge.ts:219 forwards only {type,id,timestamp} to observeCoreEvent, dropping any payload. A clean fix needs all three files; only runtime-state.ts is owned here, so this is reported, not patched.

multiAgentFourStepLive.note: Two subagents (A, B) driven by REAL SubagentStart/SubagentStop hook payloads through the REAL relay binary (kai-hook.exe) over the REAL pipe. No setTimeout trigger.

steps.expected: DELEGATING (a lone subagent is delegation, per the unit test)

steps.event: SubagentStop(A) while B still runs — THE CRITICAL STEP
steps.expected: REMAINS MULTI_AGENT (a naive counter would drop to DELEGATING here)

steps.event: SubagentStop(B) — the last live subagent stops

multiAgentFourStepLive.verdict: END-TO-END PROVEN. Step 3 (A stops while B runs) held MULTI_AGENT live — the exact case the naive per-event counter failed. The machine treats a lone subagent (step 1) as DELEGATING, not MULTI_AGENT; that is the shipped, unit-pinned behaviour ('A starts -> MULTI_AGENT' would itself be the naive-counter bug).

offlineVerdict.detail: Killed the Core (pid 10412). OFFLINE observed 1569ms later (inside the 1.5s grace + poll interval), conn='OFFLINE', pose='sleeping', with the visible note 'KAI Core is not running — reconnecting…'. The character fell offline and did NOT remain in a mid-task pose. The Core supervisor respawned it (pid 7492); the stream reconnected and the machine recovered to IDLE (char-idle.png).

recoveringVerdict.detail: Genuinely unreachable from the real stream today — see the RECOVERING state record. The Core's recovery signal is published as 'notification.created', for which stateForEvent has no case; and the payload carrying the recovery type is dropped by core-state.ts (CoreEventRow has no payload field) and again by core-bridge.ts (forwards only type/id/timestamp). Reported as a real finding.
